function: Codebook-based transmit/receive beam selection with option-based hierarchical RL to maximize radar target detection probability P_D in a bi-static MIMO-DFRC system (p. 5, 7).
system: Bi-static MIMO-DFRC: two BSs, each with 32-antenna ULA and hybrid analog beamforming (1 RF chain), one point-like target, no RIS; 28 GHz (p. 3, 9).
method: Option-based hierarchical RL (semi-MDP; over-option, intra-option, termination policies) with invalid action masking; policy networks of three hidden layers (64, 64, 16); 100 training episodes (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Custom radar-echo simulator (steering vectors, LS-estimated amplitude, clutter and noise); target coordinates uniform in U(0, 100); no dataset or measurement (p. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Same simulated geometry and random target positions; transmit power (36-45 dBm) and PFA are swept; separate two-layer and three-layer codebook cases; no unseen-condition test (p. 9-11).
baselines: Learned: original DQN, Dueling DQN, SARSA, SAC, DDPG, TD3 (discrete versions). Classical: hierarchical beam training with full five-layer and two- or three-layer codebooks (p. 9-10).
metrics: Number of steps to find the optimal beam pair and average cumulative reward (based on detection probability P_D) versus transmit power and PFA (p. 10-11).
complexity: Inference FLOPs of the two policy networks: 32|S|+16|Omega|+32(|S|+1)+16|A|+14336; exhaustive-search complexity orders given for comparison; no runtime (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "We consider a simplified distributed massive MIMO-DFRC" - custom echo model with steering vectors (eqs. 1-5) and random target positions; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "In order to evaluate the generalization of the proposed" - Fig. 4c only swaps the DRL backbone; pp. 10-11 sweep transmit power and PFA, with no model tested in a new scenario.

q4_support: p. 8: "the proposed HRL model, the total number of FLOPS during" - inference FLOPs expression of the policy networks (Section III-E).
q5_support: p. 9: "The parameters are list in Table II." - self-generated simulation run in PyTorch; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Borderline on function: the learned objective is radar target detection P_D only (p. 5: 'maximize sensing performance'; no communication metric or user in the model, p. 3), but the system is a bi-static MIMO-DFRC network of communication BSs that reuse communication codebooks (p. 1: 'employ the communication beams to detect'), so it is treated as ISAC beam selection (area 5) and not as sensing alone in a system that does not communicate. Reviewer to confirm. q3 counts the original DQN, Dueling DQN, SARSA, SAC, DDPG and TD3 applied directly to the beam selection as standard learned baselines (the proposed algorithm is integrated with each), and hierarchical beam training as the non-learned baseline, compared on the number of steps.
